The real-dataset workbench: ~31,000 genes × ~83,000 libraries of splice-junction
counts, the dataset the performance queue (`docs/scaling.md`) was built for.
This notebook is the test bed for developing WADE against it and the showcase
of the result boundary — **the data live in Dropbox and stay there**; nothing
patient-derived is written into the repository, and results land next to the
data.

Two rules it inherits:

* **Memory is budgeted, not discovered.** A full-cohort run at this shape was
  measured at **55.6 GB peak** on the synthetic twin (`docs/scaling.md` §1),
  on top of nothing — the loaders below never materialize more than they say,
  and the full-matrix path is behind an explicit gate.
* **The default render is small.** It runs one real contrast on a
  column-selected slice (~0.8 GB) end to end — load, align, test, read,
  write — in a few minutes.

## The data

```{python}
#| label: paths
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

import wade

DATA = Path("/Users/mkiyer/University of Michigan Dropbox/MED-mctp-iyerlab"
            "/projects/cfrna/rna100k_rnaseq_data")
META = Path("/Users/mkiyer/University of Michigan Dropbox/MED-mctp-iyerlab"
            "/projects/rna100k/metadata_harmonization/cache")

COUNTS_FEATHER = DATA / "cohort_sj_counts.feather"     # splice-junction counts
GENES_XLSX = DATA / "cohort_genes.xlsx"                # row annotation, incl. the normalizer
SAMPLES_PARQUET = META / "harmonized_samples.parquet"  # curated library metadata

RESULTS = DATA / "wade_results"                        # results live beside the data

#: Run the full 31k x 83k cohort. Needs ~60 GB free (measured 55.6 GB peak at
#: this shape plus the load); leave False unless you have it.
FULL_RUN = False
```

Splice-junction counts over the gene's **intron count** is the sjTPM
normalization (`wade.tpm_like`'s docstring names exactly this pair), so the
gene table supplies both the row labels and the normalizer. `gene_id` is the
unique key; `gene_name` is for reading.

```{python}
#| label: genes
genes = pl.read_excel(GENES_XLSX)
NORMALIZER = genes["gene_num_introns"].to_numpy().astype(np.float64)
assert NORMALIZER.min() >= 1, "a zero-intron gene would break the normalizer"
GENE_IDS = genes["gene_id"].to_numpy()
print(f"{genes.height:,} genes; normalizer = gene_num_introns "
      f"(min {int(NORMALIZER.min())}, median {int(np.median(NORMALIZER))})")
```

The harmonized metadata covers the whole rna100k effort; the cohort matrix's
columns are the `library` keys. A handful of cohort libraries have no
harmonized row yet — surfaced here rather than silently dropped, because a
contrast can only use libraries the curation covers.

```{python}
#| label: samples
cohort_libs = pl.scan_ipc(COUNTS_FEATHER).collect_schema().names()
samples = (pl.scan_parquet(SAMPLES_PARQUET)
             .filter(pl.col("library").is_in(cohort_libs))
             .collect())
unmatched = len(cohort_libs) - samples.height
print(f"cohort libraries: {len(cohort_libs):,}; harmonized: {samples.height:,}; "
      f"not yet harmonized: {unmatched}")
print(samples["specimen_type"].value_counts().sort("count", descending=True).head(6))
```

## Loading counts, by the column

The matrix is Int32 on disk. `load_counts` reads **only the named libraries**,
in blocks, into a preallocated float64 array — so a 3,000-sample contrast
costs ~0.8 GB and never touches the other 80,000 columns, and the full-cohort
load peaks at the array itself (20.6 GB) plus one block.

```{python}
#| label: loader
def load_counts(libraries: list[str], block: int = 4096) -> np.ndarray:
    """(genes x libraries) float64 counts for the named libraries."""
    out = np.empty((genes.height, len(libraries)), dtype=np.float64)
    scan = pl.scan_ipc(COUNTS_FEATHER)
    for s in range(0, len(libraries), block):
        cols = libraries[s:s + block]
        out[:, s:s + len(cols)] = scan.select(cols).collect().to_numpy()
    return out
```

## A first contrast: malignant vs non-malignant plasma

Plasma cfRNA is the lab's home question, and the cohort has 1,343 malignant
vs 1,662 non-malignant plasma libraries (pancreas-heavy on the malignant
side). **This is a plumbing-and-showcase contrast, not a discovery claim**:
the plasma libraries span several studies, so study and disease are partly
confounded and label exchangeability across studies is exactly the kind of
assumption `docs/limits.md` warns about. A defensible analysis would permute
within study; this notebook's job is to exercise the machinery on real data.

```{python}
#| label: contrast
plasma = samples.filter(
    (pl.col("specimen_type") == "plasma") & pl.col("is_malignant").is_not_null()
)
print(plasma["is_malignant"].value_counts(), "\n")
print(plasma.filter(pl.col("is_malignant"))["oncotree_lineage"]
      .value_counts().sort("count", descending=True).head(5))

libs = plasma["library"].to_list()
counts = load_counts(libs)
print(f"\ncounts: {counts.shape}, {counts.nbytes / 2**30:.2f} GB; "
      f"zero fraction {float((counts == 0).mean()):.2f}")
```

The condition comes from the metadata **by name** — `wade.condition` aligns
the assignment to the matrix's columns strictly and raises on any mismatch.

```{python}
#| label: run
#| warning: false
import time

cond = wade.condition(plasma, key="library", column="is_malignant",
                      case=True, control=False)

t0 = time.perf_counter()
res = wade.wade(
    counts, NORMALIZER, cond,
    gene_names=GENE_IDS, sample_names=libs,
    nperms=2000, seed=1,
    gene_chunk=4000,           # bounded memory, bit-identical (scaling.md §2.2)
    fit_backend="rust",        # opt-in fit kernel (scaling.md §3.3)
)
print(f"wade() on {counts.shape[0]:,} genes x {len(libs):,} plasma libraries: "
      f"{time.perf_counter() - t0:.0f} s   (m = {res.nprobs})")
```

(`stage1="gemm"` is not used: 1,343 v 1,662 is unbalanced, and the GEMM
identity only holds for equal groups — the default grid path covers it.)

## Reading the result

```{python}
#| label: toptable
frame = (res.to_frame()
         .join(genes.select("gene_id", "gene_name", "gene_type"),
               left_on="gene", right_on="gene_id")
         .sort("padj_subset"))
sig_mean = int((res.padj_mean_shift <= 0.05).sum())
sig_subset = int((res.padj_subset <= 0.05).sum())
print(f"BH 0.05: {sig_mean:,} mean-shift genes, {sig_subset:,} subset genes")
frame.select("gene_name", "gene_type", "log2_fc", "padj_mean_shift",
             "padj_subset", "affected_fraction", "direction").head(15)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Both stages. Left: the ordinary test. Right: 'a global shift does not explain this'."
wade.plot_volcano(res, stage="both", label=6)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-stages
#| fig-cap: "What kind of difference: the two stages against each other, coloured by affected_fraction."
wade.plot_stages(res)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-gene
#| fig-cap: "The most subset-like significant gene, in full: quantile pair, difference, log-ratio curve."
top = frame.filter(pl.col("padj_subset") <= 0.05).head(1)
wade.plot_gene(res, gene=top["gene"].to_list() if top.height else [0])
```

Two honesty checks worth keeping in view on a cohort this size:

```{python}
#| label: diagnostics
# 1. The p-value floor (scaling.md §4): at ~31k genes, BH needs resolution
#    near the empirical/GPD floor, and genes piling up there stop ranking.
floor = 1.0 / (2000 * 250)
at_floor = int((res.p_mean_shift <= floor * 1.001).sum())
print(f"mean-shift p-values at the resolution floor: {at_floor:,} "
      f"({at_floor / len(res.gene):.1%} of genes)")

# 2. Depth by group: library sizes span ~0.8M-90M in this cohort. Depth that
#    is group-associated is a batch confound no normalization removes.
depth = counts.sum(axis=0)
case = np.asarray(res.cond) == 1
print(f"median depth  malignant {np.median(depth[case]) / 1e6:.1f}M   "
      f"non-malignant {np.median(depth[~case]) / 1e6:.1f}M")
```

Results and the manifest go **beside the data**, never into the repository:

```{python}
#| label: write
RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
out = wade.write_results(res, RESULTS / "plasma_malignant_vs_nonmalignant.tsv")
print("wrote", out.name, "and", out.with_suffix("").with_suffix(".manifest.json").name)
```

## The full cohort, when you mean it

The gate, not a default: ~20.6 GB for the matrix plus WADE's residents —
**measured 55.6 GB peak at this exact shape** on the synthetic twin
(`docs/scaling.md` §1, ~30 min at B = 2,000 with `fit_backend="rust"` and,
on a balanced design, `stage1="gemm"`). Edit the contrast; the template runs
whatever the metadata can define.

```{python}
#| label: full
if FULL_RUN:
    chosen = samples.filter(
        (pl.col("specimen_type") == "tissue")
        & pl.col("sample_class").is_in(["tumor", "normal_adjacent"])
    )
    libs_full = chosen["library"].to_list()
    counts_full = load_counts(libs_full)
    cond_full = wade.condition(chosen, key="library", column="sample_class",
                               case="tumor", control="normal_adjacent")
    res_full = wade.wade(counts_full, NORMALIZER, cond_full,
                         gene_names=GENE_IDS, sample_names=libs_full,
                         nperms=2000, seed=1, gene_chunk=2000,
                         fit_backend="rust")
    wade.write_results(res_full, RESULTS / "tissue_tumor_vs_normal_adjacent.tsv")
else:
    print("FULL_RUN = False — flip it with ~60 GB free.")
```

## Reading the smoke run honestly

The first render of this notebook (2026-08-20) found **most of the
transcriptome "subset-significant"** on the plasma contrast, with **18.8% of
genes at the mean-shift p-value floor** and a **1.7× group-associated depth
difference** (malignant median 8.1M vs non-malignant 4.8M splice-junction
counts). Read together, that is not a discovery — it is the caveat at the
top of the contrast section made quantitative. At n ≈ 3,000 the test can
resolve tiny distributional differences, and this contrast bundles study,
protocol and sequencing depth with disease; the subset stage is faithfully
reporting that a single global shift does not explain group differences that
are substantially technical. The three follow-ups this motivates, in order:

* **Depth as a confound, measured** — group-associated depth is exactly the
  batch structure `docs/limits.md` warns permutation cannot absolve. The
  planned experiment (planted depth imbalance between groups; false-positive
  rates for both stages; candidate guards including depth-equalizing
  binomial thinning) belongs in `docs/scaling.md` beside the other measured
  questions.
* **Within-study contrasts** — the defensible analyses here hold study (and
  ideally protocol) fixed: single-study case/control designs, or restricted
  permutation within study, which the machinery does not yet offer.
* **P-value resolution** (`scaling.md` §4) — 18.8% of genes at the floor is
  the pile-up that section predicts; ranking has degraded and the
  saddlepoint / multilevel work now has an observed motivation, not a
  hypothetical one.

And two facts for the performance roadmap: **47% zeros** (real sparsity,
but not single cell's >90% — the §5.1 zero-run walk would roughly halve the
subset stage, not decimate it), and **depth spanning 0.8M–89M** across the
cohort, 17× between the 5th and 95th percentiles.
